title: WMPO: World Model-based Policy Optimization for Vision-Language-Action Models
claim: Existing paradigms each lack key capabilities such as learning from failures or sample efficiency; ours uses a learned world model to get all of them.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, dashed dividers, ✗/✓ capability checklists
description: Three side-by-side panels separated by dashed vertical lines, labeled (a) Imitation Learning, (b) Real World RL, (c) WMPO. Each panel has a robot-arm icon labeled VLA at the bottom and a photo mosaic with yellow-highlighted text labels such as Human Demonstration, Real World, Robotic Trajectories and Policy Behavior Data. Panel (a) shows a joystick feeding demonstrations into the VLA, with red ✗ marks for failure learning and self-correction. Panel (b) shows a Reward/Action loop between the VLA and the real world, with two green ✓ and two red ✗ marks. Panel (c) replaces the real world with a globe icon labeled World Model, fed by robotic trajectories and policy data, and shows all four green ✓ marks. Red and green checklists carry the contrast, so the eye goes to them first.
caption: Three different VLA training paradigms: (a) Imitation learning learns from human demonstrations but lacks the ability for learning from failures and self-correction; (b) Real-world RL improves policy through direct interaction but suffers from high sampling costs and difficulty in achieving on-policy RL; (c) WMPO pretrains a world model on large-scale robotic trajectories and fine-tunes it with limited policy behavior data, enabling sample-efficient on-policy RL for VLA without real-world interaction.
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown strong potential for general-purpose robotic manipulation, but their reliance on expert demonstrations limits their ability to learn from failures and perform self-corrections. Reinforcement learning (RL) addresses these through self-improving interactions with the physical environment, but suffers from high sample complexity on real robots. We introduce World-Model-based Policy Optimization (WMPO), a principled framework for on-policy VLA RL without interacting with the real environment. In contrast to widely used latent world models, WMPO focuses on pixel-based predictions that align the "imagined" trajectories with the VLA features pretrained with web-scale images. Crucially, WMPO enables the policy to perform on-policy GRPO that provides stronger performance than the often-used off-policy methods. Extensive experiments in both simulation and real-robot settings demonstrate that WMPO (i) substantially improves sample efficiency, (ii) achieves stronger overall performance, (iii) exhibits emergent behaviors such as self-correction, and (iv) demonstrates robust generalization and lifelong learning capabilities.
